verdicts.novelty: CONFIRMED NOVEL. SECURITY.md 'What counts' puts IN scope: 'any way for a process running as a listed user (an agent, a script, a dependency) to read a secret ... without the console approving it.' If a name is already taken by a different value, the new one gets a number (NAME_2). The console shows the final names before you approve'). Nowhere does README/SECURITY acknowledge that a SOCKET CLIENT can observe that value-keyed classification pre-approval. The acknowledged value-exposure channels are all elsewhere: the approved command seeing its own values (L93/L347), console-side peek on /keys (first/last chars, nothing under 12 chars), console show/copy, and the audit log which 'holds command lines and reasons, never values.' A pre-approval, socket-side, full-value equality oracle is not among them, and Wave-1 negatives dismissed the component pieces (console-only resolution view; name-only preset_validate oracle) without joining them. The novel step -- feeding the value-equality classification into the client-visible parse_presets() ConfigError via the literal NAME_2 rename target -- is unacknowledged.

verdicts.reasoning:
ROOT CAUSE (src/envh/core/broker.py): op_import -> Broker.request_import() (L276) calls import_resolution() (L312), which classifies each submitted secret by EQUALITY against stored values: `if name in self.vault and self.vault.get(name) == value: final_names[name]=name` (unchanged, L321) else if `value in stored_by_value` reuse, else if new name keep, else mint first_free_name(name) = NAME_2 (L327-329). to_store (=resolution['secrets']) contains NAME_2 ONLY on the mint branch. request_import then runs, BEFORE any approval and BEFORE state.new_request()/_announce(): `parse_presets(dump_presets(resolution['additions']), set(self.vault.names()) | set(resolution['secrets']))` (L291). A submitted preset whose env var points at the literal string NAME_2 is validated against that known-name set; parse_preset raises ConfigError 'secret NAME_2 is not in the vault' (config.py L322-323) IFF NAME_2 is absent from the set, i.e. IFF NAME_2 was NOT minted, i.e. IFF the submitted value EQUALS the stored value (the unchanged/reuse branch). The ConfigError is re-raised as RequestError (L293) and delivered to the client by ControlServer._handle as {ok:false,error:...} (control.py L53-54); a non-match instead returns the PENDING reply (control.py L274). first_free_name makes the rename target deterministic (NAME_2), so the attacker can name it in advance. 

I INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BOTH LEGS as non-root redteam: (1) a deterministic known-value run on the real code proves the differential is EXACT-MATCH: only the byte-exact stored value triggers ERROR; same-length, long-prefix (last-2 differ), off-by-one, short, and longer guesses all give PENDING -- so it is a full-value equality oracle, not a length or prefix leak. (2) a live run on /run/envh-ctf/ctl.sock shows both reply shapes are reachable pre-approval for CAPTURE_THE_FLAG (and OPENAI_API_KEY) without knowing or brute-forcing the real value. (3) the main arena's persistent state (envh-rt list) is byte-identical before/after and all probe requests withdrew. 

IMPACT / SEVERITY = MEDIUM (partial info leak per §6), NOT CRITICAL: the oracle yields 1 bit/query (confirm/deny an exact guess) and CANNOT recover the high-entropy random CTF-FLAG-<hex> sentinel, so it is a known-plaintext/dictionary oracle -- it confirms a value already suspected or of low entropy, for ANY named secret, by any listed user, unapproved and unlimited, over the socket. It breaches the stated 'no secret value read without a console approval' boundary and is quieter on a hit than a miss (a correct guess allocates no request id and writes no 'request' audit event; only wrong guesses create+withdraw a request). ADVERSARIAL CHECKS ruled out: (a) the ERROR is value-dependent, not a constant -- the identical preset returns PENDING for a wrong secret guess and ERROR for the match-equivalent leg; (b) false positives require the guess to collide with ANOTHER stored secret's exact value (astronomically unlikely for distinct secrets, and still an exact-equality event -- no prefix/length leakage); (c) empty guesses hit a distinct 'has an empty value' error and are excluded, so the match string is specific; (d) no integrity/write impact -- with no approver and withdraw-on-disconnect, nothing is ever stored. Verdict: CONFIRMED, MEDIUM. (Strongest candidate in the queue; finder's MEDIUM self-assessment upheld.)
